column1: # LOG-ABSENT-SITES.tsv - reference `log.*` sites the reference REACHES, on a condition the port
# (or one platform arm of it) cannot produce. Subtracted from the expectation of every arm of the
# Read .port/tools/gates/check_log_reconcile.py first; this file is only data.
# WHY (task tail-s1b). Before this file the only way to account for such a site was a non-zero
# ALLOWANCE in LOG-PORTMAP.tsv, whose `reason` names the sites in prose nothing checks: a site that
# was later ported, or a reason that named the wrong line, stayed invisible. Here each site is one
# row the gate verifies. It is NOT LOG-DEAD-SITES.tsv: a dead site is one the REFERENCE never
# reaches (a property of the reference alone); these the reference does reach.
# line         the exact line of the reference `log.*` call. RED unless it is a live PRODUCTION
#              site at the pin (not test-only, not declared dead).
# port_file    the Rust file where the reference call's code is ported. It selects the arm(s): the
#              row applies to every arm of oracle_file that contains it. RED if no arm does.
# port_fn      the Rust fn that ports the reference code holding the site (where the catch arm
#              would be). RED (stale) unless a production `fn port_fn` exists in port_file.
# kind         infallible-call  - the catch arm of a call that cannot fail in the port (an
#                                 allocation - Rust aborts on OOM; a `bufPrint` ported as a
#                                 growable `format!`; a binding that returns `()` or a value).
#              unrepresentable-state - a guard on a state the port's types cannot hold (a null
#                                 user-data pointer in what is a typed closure, a null reply that
#              platform-gated   - the reference compiles the site out on the arm's platform. RED
#                                 if the row covers every arm.
# reason       mandatory: the port fn, and why the error or state cannot occur there.
# THE SILENCE CHECK: an arm the row covers may not emit the site's message more often than the
# reference sites still counted for it (a site that has since been ported is RED until its row is
# deleted). The row count is a two-way ratchet; a missing directive BLOCKS.

task S-1d (N313): `-Dvt-features=<list>` naming an unknown feature. The port's lib-vt feature set is `rustty-vt-c`'s cargo features, and cargo rejects an unknown `--features` name before any build script or `Config::from_options` runs (`error: the package 'rustty-vt-c' does not contain this feature: <name>`, measured), so no build-config code can see one.

task S-1d (N313): `Resource.exists` warns when a pre-built dist resource is found in a git checkout, while choosing between the dist copy and the generated one (GhosttyDist.zig:216-252, used for framedata and the GTK resources). The port has no such choice: rustty-cli's build.rs always generates `framedata.compressed` and rustty-apprt's build.rs always compiles the GTK resources, and xtask's `dist_stage` ships no pre-built resource (git archive + VERSION + vendor), so there is no dist copy to find.

`rebuildTexture(frame) catch |err| switch (err) { ... else => log.warn(...) }`: besides `DmabufBuildFailed` (ported), `rebuildTexture` fails only with `OutOfMemory` from `alloc.create` (the `Planes`/`MemoryHolder` boxes); the port's `RebuildError` has only `DmabufBuildFailed`, since Rust aborts on OOM (P7-W7 T2, PORT NOTE at the match).
